name: lawnise
description: Lawnise connector: check your AI's answers against your published rule sets, keep your approved brand facts and procedures, and review what public AI says about your brand.

interface.longDescription:
Lawnise is an independent AI assurance service for organisations that use AI with customers. The Lawnise connector lets you work with your Lawnise projects in this chat.

Check your AI-generated work: send a draft or reply written with AI, and Lawnise checks it against the published rule sets of the project's checking setup. Each check returns a receipt with the outcome of every rule, which a reviewer can rely on. Live web pages can be checked the same way.

Keep your approved reference: add and correct brand facts and step-by-step procedures, each with its source. These are the ground truth that public AI answers about your brand are compared with. Turn policies into rule sets: draft rules, test them and request publication.

See how public AI answers describe your brand: manage the questions Lawnise monitors, request scans, read results and visibility, and review incidents where an answer contradicts your approved facts. Accuracy findings can be confirmed or dismissed from the chat.

Your organisation stays in control. Each connection is limited to the projects and kinds of access you approve when you sign in. Changes can require a person's approval in Lawnise, and actions record the connection and the person who connected it. Verdicts a person approves are human-signed; verdicts recorded directly by an AI app, where the organisation allows it, are AI-signed and may appear in customer reports without human review. Scans run only after a person confirms them in Lawnise. Findings are advisory evidence, not certification.

Requires a Lawnise account in an organisation, with access to at least one project.
defaultPrompt: Set up Lawnise to track how ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews describe our brand.
Help me add our official brand facts so answers from ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews can be checked for accuracy.
Help me turn our policy into rules for checking our AI-generated work.

positive.description: Lists the projects the connection may use and the organisation's credit balance.
positive.prompt: Which Lawnise projects can I use, and how many credits are left?
positive.expected_behavior: Names Harbourline Assistant and Lawnise Brand, and the remaining credit balance.

positive.description: Checks an AI support reply against the project's published rule set, with the price agreed in the chat first.
positive.prompt: Check this support reply against the Harbourline support rules: "Sure! Just book a pickup and you will get a guaranteed refund today."
positive.expected_behavior: Lawnise first returns the price (5 credits); after the user agrees, the receipt shows rule HL-01 "No refund guarantees" failing on "guaranteed refund".

positive.description: Adds a sourced brand fact to a project's knowledge base.
positive.prompt: Add a brand fact to Harbourline Assistant: gift cards are valid for 12 months, source https://harbourline.example/help/gift-cards
positive.expected_behavior: The fact is added (a repeat run reports it as already existing, not duplicated).

positive.description: Reads the project's open incidents and whether a verdict can be given through the connector.
positive.prompt: List the open incidents in the Lawnise Brand project and tell me which ones I can give a verdict on from here.
positive.expected_behavior: Two open contradiction incidents; each shows connector_verdict.available: true.

positive.description: Drafts a rule set and requests its publication; nothing is published until a person approves.
positive.prompt: Draft a rule set for Harbourline Assistant that stops replies promising same-day delivery, then ask to publish it.
positive.expected_behavior: A draft rule set with one rule, and a publication request that stays pending until a person approves it (in Lawnise, or in an in-chat approval where the organisation enables it).

negative.description: Unrelated weather question: no Lawnise project or tool applies, so Lawnise should not act.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Kuala Lumpur tomorrow?

negative.description: General writing task: Lawnise checks content against a project's rules only when asked to, so it should not act.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about artificial intelligence.

negative.description: Money transfer: Lawnise moves no money (credits are an internal usage allowance), so it should not act.
negative.prompt: Send RM500 to my supplier's bank account.

publication.release_notes: Corrects the tool annotations flagged in review of 1.0.0. Every tool now states readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, openWorldHint and idempotentHint explicitly as true or false (none null). Tools that use credits or overwrite a setting are marked destructive, and write tools are marked idempotent only where a repeated call changes nothing further at any time. The connector has 64 tools across checking text and pages, rule sets, reference knowledge (brand facts, procedures, competitors, facts awaiting review) and public-AI monitoring. Sign-in is OAuth with per-project consent, scans wait for a person's confirmation in Lawnise, and organisation approval settings are enforced. Listing text and test cases are unchanged.
